bg-04-01.hint: It is suddenly raining outside the window.
bg-04-01.why: Use 이/가 when reporting a newly observed fact or immediate event: 비가 와요.

bg-04-01.q: Answer that you ordered the meal using 제가 and 주문했어요.
bg-04-01.why: When answering 'Who did this?' (누가), specify the subject with 제가 (저 + 가).

bg-04-01.hint: When answering 'Who' (누가?), identify the specific subject using 제가 instead of topic marker 저는.
bg-04-01.why: Answering an information question '누가?' requires subject marker 이/가: 제가 샀어요.

steps.en: Outside the window, it suddenly rains.

ko: 창밖을 보니 갑자기 하얀 눈이 내려요.
교실 안에서는 벨 소리가 울리고 학생들이 들어왔어요.
선생님이 '누가 발표할까요?'라고 물었어요. 제가 손을 들었어요.
en: Looking out the window, white snow is suddenly falling.
Inside the classroom, a bell rang and the students came in.
The teacher asked, 'Who will present?' I raised my hand.

bg-04-01.q: What is suddenly falling outside the window?
bg-04-01.why: The text begins '창밖을 보니 갑자기 하얀 눈이 내려요'.

bg-04-01.q: What did the writer do when the teacher asked who would present?
bg-04-01.why: The text says '제가 손을 들었어요' (I raised my hand).

items: Use subject particle 이/가 for newly noticed sensory facts and events
Answer '누가?' (Who?) questions correctly with 제가 instead of 저는

bg-04-02.hint: As for me, I like apples (contrast implied).
bg-04-02.why: 은/는 highlights the topic (저는) or sets up a contrast (사과는).

bg-04-02.q: Contrast something you like with something you don’t, using 은/는 and -지만 (e.g. coffee vs tea).
bg-04-02.why: Using 은/는 on both items creates a clear contrast between coffee and tea.

bg-04-02.wrong: 저는 사과는 좋아해요. 하지만 배가 안 좋아해요.
answers: 저는 사과는 좋아해요. 하지만 배는 안 좋아해요.
저는 사과는 좋아해요. 하지만 배는 안 좋아해요
저는 사과를 좋아해요. 하지만 배는 안 좋아해요.
저는 사과를 좋아해요. 하지만 배는 안 좋아해요
bg-04-02.hint: When contrasting two different items (사과 vs 배), replace the subject particle with the contrast marker 은/는.
bg-04-02.why: Contrasting two objects requires the contrast marker 은/는: 사과는 좋아해요. 하지만 배는 안 좋아해요.

steps.en: As for me, I like apples.
I like apples, but I dislike pears.

ko: 제 친구와 저는 음식 입맛이 서로 달라요.
친구는 매운 음식을 잘 먹지만 저는 매운 음식은 전혀 못 먹어요.
하지만 달콤한 디저트는 둘 다 아주 좋아해요.
en: My friend and I have different tastes in food.
My friend eats spicy food well, but as for me, I cannot eat spicy food at all.
However, as for sweet desserts, both of us like them very much.

bg-04-02.q: How do the writer and their friend compare regarding spicy food?
options: The friend eats it well, but the writer cannot eat it
Both eat spicy food every day
bg-04-02.why: The text states '친구는 매운 음식을 잘 먹지만 저는 매운 음식은 전혀 못 먹어요'.

bg-04-02.q: What kind of food do both people enjoy together?
bg-04-02.why: The text says '하지만 달콤한 디저트는 둘 다 아주 좋아해요'.

items: Use 은/는 to establish conversation topics and introduce yourself or others
Use 은/는 to express comparisons and contrasts between two things
